normalize: normalize(x): recursive. Strings: CRLF/CR -> LF; U+00A0 -> space; rtrim each line; trim. Lists/maps: same order, values normalized.
reduce: reduce(stored) = for each stored item, q = trim(item.question ?? item.q ?? ""), a = trim(item.answer ?? item.a ?? ""); drop items where q or a is empty (faqPageSchema skips them); emit {question: q, answer: strip_tags(a)}. This is exactly the JSON-LD the live page emits.
op: Per slug: (1) if normalize(reduce(stored)) === normalize(new_faqs) -> skip "already at target". (2) elif normalize(reduce(stored)) !== normalize(old_faqs_guard) -> WARNING "old mismatch" + 200-char excerpt, write nothing. (3) else build the write value from the STORED array: same items in the same order; for each index in replace_indices, replace that stored item with new_faqs[index] (keys question/answer); every other stored item is kept byte-for-byte (C items stay exactly as stored, including any HTML). Assert normalize(reduce(result)) === normalize(new_faqs) before saveQuietly(); otherwise throw (rolls back the slug). If the stored array contains items dropped by reduce() (empty q/a), keep them in place and report the count. replace_indices refer to positions in reduce(stored); map them back to stored positions.

old_faqs_guard.question: Why is Ipamorelin considered selective?
old_faqs_guard.answer: Unlike other GH secretagogues, Ipamorelin stimulates growth hormone release without significantly increasing cortisol, prolactin, or ACTH, making it the most selective GHSR agonist available.

old_faqs_guard.question: When is the best time to inject Ipamorelin?
old_faqs_guard.answer: Approximately 1-1.5 hours after the last meal, ideally at bedtime, to align with the body's natural nocturnal GH secretion.

old_faqs_guard.question: How does Ipamorelin differ from GHRP-6?
old_faqs_guard.answer: Ipamorelin does not stimulate appetite (no ghrelin-like hunger spike) and produces a cleaner GH pulse without elevating cortisol.

new_faqs.question: Why is Ipamorelin considered selective?
new_faqs.answer: The term comes from a 1998 study in rats and swine by its developer, Novo Nordisk (developer-affiliated; Raun et al., Eur J Endocrinol 1998, PMID 9849822). Ipamorelin, a pentapeptide that acts at the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor, released GH with potency similar to GHRP-6. In swine, GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 raised ACTH and cortisol, while ipamorelin did not raise them to levels significantly different from those after GHRH, even at more than 200 times the amount needed for half-maximal GH release; none of the compounds changed FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH. That is selectivity relative to older GHRPs in animals. It is not a human finding and does not make ipamorelin the “most selective” compound available.

new_faqs.question: Has ipamorelin been tested in humans?
new_faqs.answer: Only in a few clinical studies, none of which led to approval. A 1999 study measured its pharmacokinetics and GH response after single intravenous infusions in healthy men (Gobburu et al., Pharm Res 1999, PMID 10496658; Novo Nordisk co-authors, developer-affiliated). A phase 2 trial sponsored by Helsinn, then developing ipamorelin (developer-affiliated), in 117 bowel-resection patients (NCT00672074) found no significant difference from placebo in its key or secondary efficacy analyses (Beck et al., Int J Colorectal Dis 2014, PMID 25331030). A second Helsinn-sponsored phase 2 trial (NCT01280344) was completed in 2014 with no posted results. No ipamorelin product is FDA-approved. FDA places ipamorelin acetate in 503B category 2 for significant safety risks, citing a published report of serious adverse events including death with intravenous use for gastric motility, and its advisory committee voted 0 yes, 12 no, 1 abstain on adding ipamorelin to the 503A bulks list on 29 October 2024. WADA prohibits it (2026 List, S2.2.4).

new_faqs.question: How does Ipamorelin differ from GHRP-6?
new_faqs.answer: Both are synthetic agonists of the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor. Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide (Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2; PubChem CID 9831659); GHRP-6 is a hexapeptide (PubChem CID 4345065). In the 1998 animal study, the two released GH with similar potency, but GHRP-6 raised ACTH and cortisol in swine and ipamorelin did not (Raun et al., PMID 9849822; developer-affiliated). We found no head-to-head human comparison as of 22 October 2026 (searches of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov), so claims of a “cleaner” GH pulse or no appetite effect in people are not established. FDA lists both GHRP-6 and ipamorelin acetate in 503B category 2, and WADA prohibits both (2026 List, S2.2.4).
